summary: Elizabeth J. Harris specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her doctorate under Ananda Guruge and Yakupitiyage Karunadasa at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and University of Kelaniya, holding posts at Westminster College (~1993–1997) and Birmingham (~2017).

Elizabeth J. Perry is a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. She studied at the University of Michigan (1970–1978) and held academic posts at the University of Washington (1986–1990) and Harvard University (~1997).

Elizabeth Morrison works in Buddhist studies and sinology. She studied under Janet Gyatso, Susan Niditch, Bernard Faure, and Carl Bielefeldt. She held posts at Amherst College (1998–1999) and Middlebury College (attested 2008).

Elizabeth Napper is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Virginia, studying under Jeffrey Hopkins, Geshe Wangyal, and Paul Groner, and served as co-director of the Tibetan Nuns Project (attested 2001–2006).
Elizabeth Stuart is a religious studies scholar who founded Theology & Sexuality. She served as Director (Direktorin) at the University of Winchester in 2021.
Elke Rogersdotter specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. She completed her PhD at Umeå University (attested 2006), supervised by Bozena Werbart, Karin Viklund, and P. Ajithprasad.
Ellen M. Raven works in Indology and history/archaeology. She held positions at the Kern Institute (attested 2003) and on the editorial board at Leiden University (attested 2018).
Elliot M. Stern is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He completed his doctoral studies at the University of Pennsylvania, earning PhD degrees dated 1988 and 1998.

Elliot Sperling (1951–2017) specialized in Tibetology, sinology, and history. Educated at CUNY Queens College and Indiana University Bloomington under Helmut Hoffmann, Thubten Jigme Norbu, and Lynn A. Struve, he taught at Indiana (1987–2015), Harvard, and Delhi.

Ellison Banks Findly specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She studied under Fred Pfeil and held positions at Mount Holyoke College and Trinity College, Hartford, where she was associate professor of religion and Asian studies (attested 1989).
Elvin A. Kabat (1914–2000) studied at Columbia University (~1934–1937). He held academic posts at Cornell University (~1938–1941) and Columbia University (~1941–1985).

Emanuel Sarkisyanz (1923–2015) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tehran and University of Chicago (PhD ~1948–1952), and became Head of the Political Science Department at Heidelberg University in 1967.
Emanuela Garatti is a scholar of Tibetology who has held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the University of Munich (attested 2018).

Embar Krishnamacharya was an Indologist. He held positions as Pandit at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library, and posts at Sanskrit Pathashala, Vadtal (attested 1937) and Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya, Vadodara (attested 1939).

Emi Matsushita is a historian and archaeologist. She studied at Nanzan University, University of East Anglia, and Ohio State University under John C. Huntington, holding posts at the Shizuoka Prefectural Board of Education (1994–1996) and Ohio State (1999–2001).

Emil Rödiger (1801–1874) was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies. Educated at Halle-Wittenberg (1821–1828), he held professorships there (1830–1860) and at Humboldt University of Berlin (from 1860), and managed the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (~1845–1853).

Emil Schlagintweit (1835–1904) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Franz Joseph Lauth and was elected a corresponding member of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 1864.

Emil Sieg (1866–1951) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Berlin, Tübingen, Munich, Kiel, and Göttingen under Albrecht Weber and Franz Kielhorn. He held professorships at Humboldt University of Berlin, Kiel University, and the University of Göttingen (from 1920).

Emilio Teza (1831–1912) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Anton Boller. He worked at the Marciana and Laurentian libraries, and served as Ordinarius at the universities of Bologna (1860), Pisa (~1862–1886), and Padua (~1886–1904).

Emily T. Yeh is a Tibetologist who earned degrees at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (1993, 1995) and the University of California, Berkeley (2003). She held a post at the University of Colorado Boulder (~2003).
